perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is a project manager whose project progress is suffering. He feels frustrated and anxious and believes his team is unmotivated.
- He met his friend Arthur Begum at a coffee shop and told Arthur that his team seemed completely unmotivated and that it was affecting progress.
- Arthur advised him to understand what drives each team member individually and to have one-on-one conversations. Harold agreed to try this and felt more hopeful.
- Harold told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Two team members said they were open to it / thought it could help. Harold said he would schedule time with each.
- After trying this, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried and told Arthur it had not worked.
- Arthur told him there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and advised digging deeper. Harold decided to hold another round of one-on-one meetings.
- In those meetings, one team member told him there was tension among a few people affecting work. Another told him they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold told them he would look into resolving conflicts and redistributing tasks, and that their well-being was important.
- Feeling optimistic and empowered, Harold told the team he would create a more supportive, open environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- Two team members responded positively. Harold said their input and well-being were crucial and urged them to work together for project success.

He does not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, narrator-only traits, or events/information he did not observe or hear.
